questions.stem: Why is carbon dioxide produced during fermentation in yeast useful in bread making?

options.text: It adds flavour to the bread
It kills harmful bacteria in the dough
It makes the dough rise by creating gas bubbles
It provides nutrients for the bread

questions.explanation: The carbon dioxide gas produced by yeast fermentation gets trapped in the dough, forming bubbles that cause the bread to rise and give it a light, airy texture.
